analysis.estimand: The ratio of cg_hist's median wall_seconds to the pooled median wall_seconds of whichever non-cg_hist baseline solver(s) the committed campaign pairs it against, computed over ok=true solves in the planted-support regime the design selects (k spanning roughly 75 up to 0.4p) across the families sparse, correlated, toeplitz, block and illcond.

execution_shape.rationale: Six plan-differing units split 5 families x 2 seeds (10 instance combinations) across three units per baseline for two baselines, each unit pairing cg_hist with one baseline at a shared lambda_ratio and tolerance with 3 repetitions, so the pooled cg_hist-vs-baseline ratio has family, seed and baseline diversity within one execution's 4-instance/2-arm cap and the campaign's 6-unit cap.

observables.description: One record per solve; restricted to ok=true to hold accuracy matched across cg_hist and baselines.
observables.name: solves

analysis.population: cg.cells@1 solves with ok=true in the five planted-support families (sparse, correlated, toeplitz, block, illcond), at whatever (n,p,k) instances, shared lambda_ratio and shared tolerance the campaign plan sets within the k~75-to-0.4p regime, comparing cg_hist against the specific baseline solver(s) -- at least two distinct baselines, out of celer/skglm/lars/sklearn/conic_reduced/conic_thesis -- that the plan actually pairs it with; this frozen analysis speaks only to the baselines and families the campaign includes, pooled together, not necessarily all six baselines individually.
analysis.target_claim: cg_hist's median wall-clock time is at least 20% below the pooled median wall-clock time of the baseline solver(s) it is run against, within the planted-support regime, across the families and seeds the campaign covers.

stated_shape.rationale: Six plan-differing units split 5 families x 2 seeds (10 instance combinations) across three units per baseline for two baselines, each unit pairing cg_hist with one baseline at a shared lambda_ratio and tolerance with 3 repetitions, so the pooled cg_hist-vs-baseline ratio has family, seed and baseline diversity within one execution's 4-instance/2-arm cap and the campaign's 6-unit cap.

hypothesis.core_idea: Replace the proposal's planned from-scratch generator and harness with the already-declared cg.cells@1 capability, which already provides a seeded, versioned, multi-family instance generator and a multi-solver wall-clock harness. Compose a plan that fixes (n, p, k) pairs so that k runs from ~75 up to 0.4p, spans the five non-historical families, pairs cg_hist against each baseline solver at a shared tolerance and lambda_ratio grid, and replicates the design across at least 4 independent seeds (RESEARCH_OS_SEED_0 offsets, combined as a campaign). Pre-register the effect-size threshold (20% median wall-clock reduction) and the majority-of-triples decision rule before running any cell, so the result cannot be narratively fit after the fact.
hypothesis.falsifier: Compose and run a cg.cells@1 campaign of at least 4 units differing only in seed (RESEARCH_OS_SEED_0), each unit's plan covering instances from families sparse, correlated, toeplitz, block, illcond with (n, p, k) chosen so k spans from ~75 to 0.4p, a shared lambda_ratio grid, a shared tolerance, and pairing solver=cg_hist against each of celer, skglm, lars, sklearn, conic_reduced, conic_thesis in turn (2 arms per unit, as the capability allows). Restrict to records with ok=true. For every (family, seed, baseline) triple, compute the median wall_seconds ratio of cg_hist to the baseline over repetitions. The pre-registered claim is falsified if, for any baseline, the ratio is not below 0.8 (i.e. cg_hist is not at least 20% faster) in a majority of its (family, seed) triples, or if the sign of the advantage (ratio above vs. below 1) is inconsistent across seeds within the same family.
hypothesis.mechanism: If cg_hist's column-generation strategy gives it a genuine computational edge in this support-size-to-feature-count regime (e.g. because it generates only the columns the active set needs, avoiding full Gram-matrix work that scales with p), that edge should reproduce as a consistent wall_seconds advantage over every baseline, in the same regime, on freshly generated instances with different seeds and across structurally different families (correlation, block, ill-conditioning) -- because the mechanism is about the solver's asymptotic work, not about the specific random draw or generator quirks of the original 2023 artifact.
hypothesis.research_question: Within the planted-support regime spanning k≈75 up to k=0.4p, does cg_hist attain a median wall_seconds at least 20% lower than each of celer, skglm, lars, sklearn, conic_reduced and conic_thesis, at matched accuracy (ok=true, comparable relative_gap), in a majority of (family, seed) combinations across the families sparse, correlated, toeplitz, block and illcond, and does that direction of advantage hold consistently across seeds rather than flipping sign?
hypothesis.title: Pre-registered wall-clock comparison of cg_hist against all declared baselines in the k=75-to-0.4p regime, using cg.cells@1
